thread.title: One Big Investor Is Buying Up Apple, Boeing, Verizon, and Intel Stock

title: One Big Investor Is Buying Up Apple, Boeing, Verizon, and Intel Stock
text:
One Big Investor Is Buying Up Apple, Boeing, Verizon, and Intel Stock By Oct. 31, 2018 7:00 a.m. ET Order Reprints Photography by Kena Betancur/AFP/Getty Images Text size
Assenagon Asset Management, of Senningerberg, Luxembourg, has a chunk of assets under management that belies the size of the country it’s based in. As of Sept. 30, Assenagon managed more than $10.1 billion in U.S.-traded securities. That’s nearly one-sixth of the total gross domestic product of Luxembourg in 2017, according to the CIA World Factbook.
Assenagon holds large positions in American stocks, and doesn’t shy away from making seemingly aggressive moves. In the third quarter, the asset manager bought nearly 1.37 million Apple (AAPL) shares, a quarter million Boeing (BA) shares, and more than a million shares of Verizon Communications (VZ). It opened large new positions in Texas Instruments (TXN) and Intel (INTC), disclosing the purchases in a Monday filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Assenagon didn’t respond to a request for comment on the trades.
The manager owned only 21,654 Apple shares at the end of the second quarter, but bulked up on the stock in the third quarter, building up a holding of 1.39 million shares by Sept. 30. The iPhone maker’s stock rallied 22% in the third quarter, excluding dividend payments, although with the recent market volatility, Apple shares are down 5.5% so far in the fourth quarter.

Assenagon bought 249,387 additional Boeing shares in the third quarter, raising its investment in the aerospace giant to 338,907 shares. Boeing shares rose 11% in the third quarter, but they have lost more than half of those gains with the recent volatility. Still, shares are up 20.4% for the year so far. Many on the Street have feared for Boeing as trade tensions continue with China, but some analysts have seen upbeat signs of late.
Verizon shares rose 7.3% in the third quarter, when Assenagon bought 1.04 million more shares of the communications giant, bringing its investment to nearly 1.08 million shares. The manager had only owned 35,816 Verizon shares at the end of the second quarter. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 6% so far in the fourth quarter, but Dow component Verizon is sporting a 10.2% gain, thanks to strong third-quarter earnings .
Texas Instruments has tumbled 13.3% so far this quarter, following a 2.1% slip in the third quarter, when Assenagon established a new position of 677,743 shares. The chip maker issued disappointing guidance a week ago, sending its stock diving. But only a month ago, Texas Instruments raised its dividend by 24%.
Assenagon initiated a position of 128,502 Intel shares in the third quarter, a period that saw the stock slip 4.3%. Intel, after surging Tuesday, has eked out a 1% gain so far in the fourth quarter. Shares also rallied last week in response to strong earnings and guidance . The stock is another Dow component that is up so far this quarter while the index is down.
